scope: Two Google Images searches, six captured result viewports, live Upbit exchange, official PC trading guide. Not an exhaustive crawl of all images on the web.

sources.purpose: Compare recurring PC structure across current guides and historical images; do not treat old third-party screenshots as current authority.
Observe mobile tab hierarchy, compact order fields, quantity shortcuts, persistent navigation.
Live navy navigation, flat white panels, gray gutters, numeric hierarchy and market directory. Second capture is chart interaction, not an order-panel capture.
Primary guide confirms price/quantity/total entry, order action and investment-history navigation.

findings.issue: Three 260px colored tiles dominate before any contract information or order inputs. A product and account/merchant shortcuts have equal visual prominence.
findings.change: Remove tiles. Show selected product price/terms in the main column with adjacent directory and subscription input.

findings.issue: Product decision and application require a second screen despite a single available product.
findings.change: Unify product context and subscription in one workspace. Make information/calculator/risk switch without losing quantity.

findings.issue: Red, pink, gradients, rounded cards and shadows compete with meaningful status and amounts.
findings.change: Navy header, neutral gray gutters, flat white panels, restrained blue active controls; no arbitrary return color.

findings.issue: Marketing tiles consume mobile space; long menu labels lack compact persistent navigation.
findings.change: Short task-based labels, mobile bottom navigation, direct jump to subscription.

findings.issue: Disabled subscription plus separate login action gives anonymous visitors two competing next steps.
findings.change: One primary guest login action. Signed users retain mandatory consents and server-side gating.

intentionalDifferences: No invented price chart, order book, trades or fake additional restaurants.
No copied Upbit wordmark or implied Upbit identity verification.
No wallet transactions or user credentials used in design research.
Original ZIP remains a historical prototype; user explicitly requested Upbit-led revision in this turn.

comparison.scaling: None; structural research only, not revised implementation QA
